prompt:
Image 1 is the layout guide: flat grey placeholder shapes on a pure black background, one for each element of this sheet. Keep every element exactly where its placeholder is, at exactly its size, and paint it as described below; no grey placeholder may remain. Copy only the layout and the sizes from Image 1, never its flat grey shading.
Image 2 is the approved painted portrait of the game's Fire Sprite, a creature of living flame: it shows how fire, embers and smoke are painted in this game. Copy its hand, its brushwork and its palette, but nothing of its subject, framing, lighting or background.
Image 3 is a painted portrait from the same game, the approved style anchor. Copy its hand, its brushwork and its palette, but nothing of its subject, framing, lighting or background.

A game effects sheet: six frames of one fireball exploding on the ground, painted on black, one frame in each cell of a 3 by 2 grid, read left to right, top row then bottom row. Each frame is centred where its grey placeholder is and is as large as it; the ground ellipse at the bottom of each placeholder is where the fire meets the ground.

Every frame is seen from the battle camera high above: the explosion is a low, wide dome of fire sitting on the ground, its base a flat ellipse, its height less than its width. Never a tall mushroom cloud, never a column of fire, never seen from the side or at eye level.
1: ignition: a small brilliant core of golden-white fire just touching the ground, a few sparks flying.
2: the burst: a low dome of orange fire bulging outward over the ground, its core blazing.
3: the full burst, the widest and brightest frame: a low dome of churning flame tongues over the whole ground ellipse, flames curling outward along the ground at its rim, sparks thrown out.
4: breaking: the dome tears open at its top, flames curl outward and down, orange and deep red, the core dimmer, the first dark smoke at its top.
5: dying: a ring of low flames running along the ground around a dark, burnt middle, a column of dark smoke rising from the middle.
6: embers: small glowing embers and flickers lying in a broken ring on the ground, a thin wisp of smoke.

Camera: the game's battle camera, high above the field and looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at miniatures on a table; orthographic, no perspective. Anything lying on the ground is foreshortened: a round shape on the ground appears as a flat ellipse about two thirds as tall as it is wide.

These sprites are light: in the game they are added onto the battle field, so anything that is not black glows and pure black disappears. Paint them as glowing fire on the black, never on a coloured or grey background; no ground, no figures, no scenery, no cast shadows.
Ember's colours: a pale golden-white to golden-yellow core (#FFE9A8 to #FFB347), an orange body (#FD6533) and deep red edges (#7A1E12) that fade into the black; dark charcoal smoke where the fire thins.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, the same hand as the painted portrait references; soft painterly edges with a few crisp strokes. Each element has a strong, simple, readable shape that still reads when it is shrunk to 20 pixels. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no glossy 3D render, no vector shapes, no airbrushed gradients, no pixel art, no photograph.

Background: perfectly flat pure black (#000000), completely uniform from edge to edge, with no texture, no vignette, no grid lines, no frames, no labels, no numbers and no text. Every element stands apart from the others with clear background between them, and none touches the edge of the image.
